title: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-003 Focused Scenario Bank v4.1

questions.stem: A SIEM timeline shows a VPN login at 02:14:08, an EDR process start at 02:11:42, and a firewall connection at 02:13:57 from the same host. The endpoint clock is later found to be 4 minutes slow. What should the analyst do FIRST before reconstructing the sequence?

options.A: Normalize event times using a trusted time reference
options.B: Discard endpoint events and use network events instead
options.C: Sort events by the timestamps originally recorded
options.D: Increase the SIEM retention period for the affected sources

questions.stem: A production API begins returning intermittent 500 errors during a suspected intrusion. Current logs record request path, status code, and client IP but not authentication context or exception details. Which change best improves investigation while limiting unnecessary exposure?

options.A: Enable packet capture around the affected API tier during a controlled diagnostic window
options.B: Enable targeted diagnostic logging for the affected service and protect the added fields
options.C: Raise logging broadly across adjacent services without defining a collection window
options.D: Disable application logging and rely on reverse-proxy access logs

questions.stem: EDR records reg.exe modifying HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run to launch %APPDATA%\sync.exe. The user denies installing software. What is the analyst's BEST interpretation?

options.A: A machine-wide service was registered and will execute before user logon
options.B: A browser proxy setting was changed and may redirect web traffic
options.C: A user-level persistence mechanism was added and the referenced binary should be investigated
options.D: A scheduled task was created and should appear in Task Scheduler logs

questions.stem: A contractor laptop connected to an office switch has valid credentials but fails device posture checks. It can reach DNS and remediation services but not engineering repositories. Which design choice most directly explains the observed access?

options.A: A flat internal network permits access after successful authentication
options.B: A site-to-site VPN isolates engineering traffic from office users
options.C: A public-key infrastructure blocks traffic from unmanaged MAC addresses
options.D: Policy-based segmentation restricts access based on identity and device posture

questions.stem: A user leaves the company. The local account is disabled, but the user can still access a SaaS application through an active federated session. Which action should the analyst prioritize?

options.A: Revoke the identity-provider session and downstream tokens
options.B: Reset the SaaS application's TLS certificate
options.C: Delete the user's workstation computer account
options.D: Remove the user's mailbox from the email retention policy

questions.stem: A domain administrator account is used interactively from several workstations, making attribution difficult. Security wants approvals, short-lived elevation, and session recording without eliminating administrative capability. Which change best fits?

options.A: Require administrators to share one vaulted domain administrator password
options.B: Move privileged activity through PAM with named accounts and time-bounded elevation
options.C: Replace domain accounts with local administrator accounts on each workstation
options.D: Route administrator traffic through a CASB before reaching Active Directory

questions.stem: A finance employee uploads a spreadsheet containing cardholder data to an unsanctioned file-sharing service from a managed laptop. Which control combination would most directly detect the SaaS use and enforce data policy?

options.A: NIDS signatures with local file integrity monitoring
options.B: PAM session recording with privileged command approval
options.C: CASB visibility with DLP inspection and policy enforcement
options.D: PKI certificate pinning with DNS reputation filtering

questions.stem: NetFlow shows one workstation connecting to 198.51.100.27 every 239 to 245 seconds for 60 to 80 bytes outbound and 140 to 170 bytes inbound. The destination has no business relationship. Which hypothesis should be investigated first?

options.A: Bulk data exfiltration over a long-lived session
options.B: A broadcast storm caused by a switching loop
options.C: Routine software distribution from an internal mirror
options.D: Jittered command-and-control beaconing

questions.stem: A firewall records a single external source sending TCP SYNs to port 445 on 2,000 internal addresses through a misconfigured ACL. Most hosts return RST and a few return SYN/ACK. What activity is best supported?

options.A: A horizontal scan for hosts exposing SMB
options.B: A vertical scan for many services on one host
options.C: An ARP sweep to enumerate local MAC addresses
options.D: A password spray against a shared authentication service

questions.stem: A Windows endpoint shows mshta.exe launched by explorer.exe, followed by powershell.exe making an HTTPS connection and creating a scheduled task. Which evidence is most useful for deciding whether this is malicious?

options.A: The fact that mshta.exe and powershell.exe are Microsoft-signed binaries
options.B: The process ancestry, command lines, destination, and task contents taken together
options.C: The presence of HTTPS because encrypted traffic is uncommon for system tools
options.D: The user account's password age and most recent successful password change

questions.stem: A Linux web server's CPU rises to 95% overnight. ps shows dozens of identical processes running from /tmp/.cache/x, and outbound traffic goes to several mining-pool domains. Which conclusion is most defensible?

options.A: A database query plan is causing application-layer latency
options.B: A vulnerability scanner is performing an authenticated assessment
options.C: Unauthorized cryptomining is consuming host resources
options.D: A log rotation job is compressing historical web logs

questions.stem: A developer workstation normally sends less than 200 MB outbound daily. It sends 18 GB overnight to a newly created cloud-storage tenant using the user's valid browser session. Which additional evidence would best distinguish exfiltration from legitimate work?

options.A: Proxy and DNS logs showing the destination and duration of the transfer
options.B: DLP events showing whether the transferred files matched protected-data rules
options.C: Project and user activity records showing whether a bulk upload to that tenant was expected
options.D: File-access records plus cloud audit events identifying the staged and uploaded objects

questions.stem: An internal payroll application creates a new API key for an account that has never used the API. Minutes later, the account enumerates employees and exports records. What should the analyst prioritize?

options.A: Validate whether the API-key creation and export were authorized for that account
options.B: Block the payroll server from resolving external DNS names
options.C: Reissue the server certificate because API keys are cryptographic material
options.D: Tune the vulnerability scanner to ignore authenticated application endpoints

questions.stem: A phishing email contains https://secure-payroll.example.com@xn--payrol-7ve.example/login. What should the analyst examine first to determine the actual destination?

options.A: The visible brand text before the at-sign because browsers prefer the first hostname
options.B: The authority portion and registrable domain after URL parsing and punycode decoding
options.C: The HTTPS scheme because encrypted links are generally authenticated to the displayed brand
options.D: The path component because /login determines which organization owns the site

questions.stem: An analyst has a 4 GB PCAP and needs to identify which TCP stream carried a suspicious HTTP POST, then reconstruct the application conversation. Which tool is the better fit for this task?

options.A: tshark with display filtering but without interactive stream reconstruction
options.B: Zeek logs summarizing the HTTP session without full payload reconstruction
options.C: Wireshark with display filters and stream reconstruction
options.D: tcpflow-style extraction of application streams without interactive packet inspection

questions.stem: A responder has SSH access to a headless Linux sensor and needs a five-minute capture of traffic to one suspicious IP without installing a GUI. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Use tshark to decode matching traffic in the terminal without saving a packet capture
options.B: Use a socket monitor to record the target process connections during the window
options.C: Use ss and connection logs to identify current sessions without capturing payloads
options.D: Use tcpdump with a host filter and write the capture to a PCAP

questions.stem: A SOC already correlates endpoint, identity, and firewall events in a SIEM. Analysts spend time enriching alerts with reputation data and opening tickets before containment approval. Which addition most directly reduces that repetitive work?

options.A: A SOAR workflow that enriches alerts, creates cases, and requests approval for containment
options.B: A case-management integration that opens tickets but leaves enrichment manual
options.C: An enrichment service that returns reputation data but does not orchestrate actions
options.D: An analyst script that enriches selected alerts but requires manual execution

questions.stem: A malicious document launches a signed Windows utility that injects into another process, then deletes the original file. Antivirus never writes a malware signature alert. Which data source is most likely to preserve the behavioral chain?

options.A: Windows event logs showing process creation but not memory or injection telemetry
options.B: EDR telemetry showing process ancestry, memory injection, and subsequent behavior
options.C: Proxy logs showing the outbound destination without the originating process chain
options.D: Antivirus logs showing scan results without behavioral process ancestry

questions.stem: A new domain appears in a phishing campaign. The analyst wants its registration date, registrar, and current name servers before deciding whether it is newly established infrastructure. Which source is most directly relevant?

options.A: Passive DNS history showing prior resolutions and hosting changes
options.B: Certificate-transparency records showing certificates issued for related hostnames
options.C: WHOIS or RDAP registration records for the domain and registrar metadata
options.D: DNS reputation records showing whether resolvers classify the domain as suspicious

questions.stem: A suspicious binary cannot be executed because the analyst is still deciding whether handling restrictions permit detonation. Which first step can reveal embedded URLs, paths, and command fragments without running it?

options.A: Open the binary in a debugger without allowing execution to proceed
options.B: Inspect imports and section metadata with a static-analysis utility
options.C: Calculate hashes and compare them with approved reputation sources
options.D: Extract printable strings and inspect metadata

questions.stem: Static review finds an obfuscated executable with no useful strings. The analyst needs registry, filesystem, process, and network behavior. Which next step best addresses the requirement?

options.A: Detonate a copy in an isolated malware sandbox with monitoring
options.B: Execute the file in a monitored virtual machine that lacks full sandbox instrumentation
options.C: Use static disassembly to infer likely behavior without observing runtime effects
options.D: Run the file under a debugger in an isolated lab and manually trace selected calls

questions.stem: A message claiming to be from invoices@vendor.example has SPF pass for bounce.mailer.example, DKIM pass for mailer.example, and DMARC fail for vendor.example. Which interpretation is strongest?

options.A: The message is authentic because SPF and DKIM each produced a passing result
options.B: The sending infrastructure authenticated, but it did not align with the visible vendor identity
options.C: The recipient mail server forged the From header because DMARC failed
options.D: The DKIM signature proves the visible vendor domain authorized the message

questions.stem: An account appears to sign in from New York and Singapore 12 minutes apart. VPN records show the user had an active session through corporate cloud-hosted VPN infrastructure during the same period. What should the analyst do next?

options.A: Disable the account because geographic distance makes compromise conclusive
options.B: Suppress the travel alert when the identity event shows successful MFA
options.C: Correlate VPN, device, session, and identity telemetry before treating the travel as compromise
options.D: Block the observed Singapore session before checking VPN egress context

questions.stem: A hunter must identify PowerShell command lines containing either -enc or -encodedcommand, regardless of case, while avoiding matches in unrelated fields. Which technique is most suitable?

options.A: Use a literal string search against the command-line field for each encoding variant
options.B: Parse the field with a small script and compare exact command tokens
options.C: Use a SIEM wildcard query over the command-line field and review the wider match set
options.D: Apply a field-scoped regular expression to the command-line data

questions.stem: A paid feed rates an IP as high confidence malicious, but the sighting is 14 months old and the address now belongs to a major cloud provider. Internal telemetry shows routine SaaS traffic. What is the best next action?

options.A: Reassess timeliness, ownership, context, and corroborating observables before blocking
options.B: Block the address because paid feeds should supersede current internal observations
options.C: Remove the entire feed because one indicator became stale
options.D: Associate other workloads at the provider with the indicator until reviewed

questions.stem: A hunter suspects credential dumping followed by remote service use. Which query set best tests the hypothesis rather than searching for known hashes?

options.A: Search antivirus alerts for files matching one malware hash from last month's incident
options.B: Look for credential-access process behavior followed by anomalous remote logons from the same hosts
options.C: List hosts missing related operating-system patches and sort by severity
options.D: Review successful MFA events without correlating endpoint or remote-service telemetry

questions.stem: A new phishing infrastructure indicator is validated during incident response. Which downstream use gives the organization the greatest immediate defensive value?

options.A: Add the indicator to the annual risk register without operational distribution
options.B: Publish the raw indicator externally before confirming handling restrictions
options.C: Share the indicator and context with detection, hunting, and blocking workflows
options.D: Use the indicator to raise CVSS scores on unrelated software vulnerabilities

questions.stem: A decoy SSH service has no legitimate users, yet one source logs in using a planted credential and attempts host discovery. How should the alert be treated?

options.A: As routine administrative activity because the authentication succeeded
options.B: As a vulnerability-management false positive until a CVE is identified
options.C: As evidence that the decoy should be promoted into a production management interface
options.D: As a high-signal indicator requiring investigation of the credential source and adjacent activity

questions.stem: The SOC wants to automate four recurring tasks. Which is the best initial candidate for unattended automation?

options.A: Enrich a new IP indicator from approved sources and add the results to its case
options.B: Disable a user account after two correlated high-confidence identity and endpoint alerts
options.C: Create a draft regulatory-notification task when an incident reaches a defined declaration state
options.D: Block a destination after one medium-confidence reputation match with no internal corroboration

questions.stem: A SOAR playbook automatically blocks domains after one low-confidence feed match and has caused several business outages. Which redesign best preserves automation while reducing risk?

options.A: Remove approval gates from disruptive containment steps to shorten response time
options.B: Require corroboration and use approval gates for disruptive actions above defined impact thresholds
options.C: Stop enriching indicators so the playbook has fewer inputs to evaluate
options.D: Increase the feed polling rate so the same low-confidence indicator appears more often

questions.stem: A ticketing platform should create a case within seconds when the SIEM marks an alert as confirmed, without polling the SIEM every minute. Which integration pattern best fits?

options.A: Export the SIEM database nightly and import it into the ticketing platform
options.B: Configure the ticketing platform to perform continuous full-text searches of archived logs
options.C: Send an authenticated webhook from the SIEM to the ticketing workflow
options.D: Mirror packet captures to the ticketing server and derive cases from raw traffic

questions.stem: Analysts switch among separate consoles for EDR, email, identity, and firewall alerts. The organization wants one operational view but does not want to replace the underlying products. What approach best meets the goal?

options.A: Replace specialized controls with a single network intrusion-prevention appliance
options.B: Disable source-system alerts after forwarding monthly summaries to management
options.C: Store screenshots from each console in a shared folder for analysts to review
options.D: Integrate telemetry and case context into a central console while retaining source-system drill-down

questions.stem: Malware uses HTTPS to a newly registered domain. The proxy sees destination and certificate metadata but not the HTTP payload. Policy permits inspection for corporate devices. Which change most directly improves content visibility?

options.A: Perform authorized TLS inspection with managed trust and defined privacy exceptions
options.B: Block HTTPS to newly observed domains until their content can be reviewed
options.C: Replace endpoint EDR with DNS logging because encrypted traffic cannot be inspected
options.D: Use a vulnerability scanner to infer HTTP request bodies from open service ports

questions.stem: A scanner sees TCP/445 and identifies Windows Server 2022 but cannot determine missing local patches or insecure registry settings. What change would most improve assessment depth?

options.A: Move the scanner outside the perimeter and repeat the same unauthenticated probes
options.B: Run an internal credentialed scan using a least-privileged assessment account
options.C: Increase the number of SYN packets sent to each discovered service
options.D: Replace active scanning with passive DNS collection for the target subnet

questions.stem: Sales laptops are often off VPN for weeks, and monthly network scans consistently miss them. Which approach best improves vulnerability coverage without requiring the devices to be on-premises?

options.A: Increase internal scanner concurrency during the monthly maintenance window
options.B: Run more external scans against the corporate public address range
options.C: Deploy managed vulnerability agents that report when the laptops have Internet access
options.D: Use passive network discovery from the data-center core switch

questions.stem: An ICS vendor warns that unsolicited probes can destabilize legacy controllers. Security still needs an initial asset inventory and exposure picture. What should the team do first?

options.A: Run a full authenticated scan at maximum speed before the next production shift
options.B: Fuzz industrial protocols from the corporate LAN to identify parser weaknesses
options.C: Install vulnerability agents on controllers after confirming basic network reachability
options.D: Use passive discovery from mirrored traffic and coordinate any later active testing with operations

questions.stem: A team wants to find hard-coded credentials and unsafe API use in source code before a release candidate is executed. Which assessment method is the best fit?

options.A: Static application analysis during the build process
options.B: Dynamic testing against the running production instance
options.C: External network scanning of the application's load balancer
options.D: Passive packet analysis of normal user sessions

questions.stem: A custom service crashes when it receives malformed length values. The developers want to systematically discover similar parser failures before release. Which approach best fits?

options.A: Compare the source repository against CIS operating-system benchmarks
options.B: Fuzz the service in a controlled test environment and monitor for crashes
options.C: Run passive asset discovery on the production subnet during business hours
options.D: Use WHOIS to identify the registrar for the service's public domain

questions.stem: A vulnerability scan finds no known CVEs on a Linux server, but an audit shows passwordless sudo for a service account and world-writable configuration files. Which assessment would most directly expose these issues?

options.A: An external port scan focused on Internet-reachable services
options.B: A malware sandbox analysis of the installed package binaries
options.C: A configuration-baseline scan against an approved hardening benchmark
options.D: A DNS reputation check for the server's configured resolvers

questions.stem: An assessor discovers an unknown host and needs to identify listening TCP services and likely service versions before choosing deeper tests. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: Masscan for high-speed discovery of open ports across large address ranges
options.B: Netcat for manual connection and banner checks against selected ports
options.C: Recon-ng for external reconnaissance and OSINT collection
options.D: Nmap with service and version detection enabled

questions.stem: A tester needs to intercept an authenticated HTTP request, modify a JSON parameter, replay it, and compare authorization responses. Which tool is the best fit?

options.A: Burp Suite or ZAP used as an intercepting web proxy
options.B: curl used to manually resend edited HTTP requests from the command line
options.C: Wireshark used to inspect captured HTTP traffic without modifying live requests
options.D: Nmap NSE scripts used to probe the service without an intercepting proxy

questions.stem: A quick assessment is needed for a newly exposed web server to identify dangerous default files, outdated server components, and common web-server misconfigurations. Which tool is the most direct starting point?

options.A: Arachni for broader web-application vulnerability scanning
options.B: Nikto for web-server checks against known dangerous files and configuration issues
options.C: ZAP for intercepting and actively testing application requests
options.D: Nmap NSE scripts for service-oriented checks against the exposed ports

questions.stem: A security team needs recurring authenticated checks for missing patches and known vulnerabilities across mixed server platforms. Which pair of tools is in the correct category for that job?

options.A: Nmap and Recon-ng
options.B: Prowler and Scout Suite
options.C: Nessus and OpenVAS
options.D: Burp Suite and ZAP

questions.stem: A researcher can reproduce a crash in a native Linux service and needs to inspect registers, stack frames, memory, and the faulting instruction. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: GDB attached to or launching the service for interactive crash analysis
options.B: objdump used to disassemble the binary without a live debugging session
options.C: A core-dump analyzer used after process termination for postmortem analysis
options.D: strace used to trace system calls without full register and memory inspection

questions.stem: A penetration tester has approval to determine whether a scanner finding is actually exploitable and needs a framework with exploit modules, payload handling, and session management. Which tool best fits?

options.A: Metasploit Framework with exploit and session modules
options.B: Nmap with NSE vulnerability scripts
options.C: Nessus with a vulnerability check for the affected service
options.D: A debugger used to reproduce the crash without exploit-session handling

questions.stem: A tester has authorized AWS credentials and must demonstrate whether existing permissions can be chained into privilege escalation. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: Prowler for AWS security and compliance checks
options.B: Pacu for AWS exploitation and privilege-escalation paths
options.C: Scout Suite for cloud configuration posture assessment
options.D: AWS Config for managed configuration-compliance rules

questions.stem: A cloud-security engineer has read-only AWS credentials and needs an open-source CLI focused on checking the account against AWS security best practices and named compliance frameworks. The task is assessment, not exploitation. Which tool best matches?

options.A: Pacu for AWS exploitation and privilege-escalation modules
options.B: Prowler for AWS security best-practice and compliance checks
options.C: Scout Suite for a broad point-in-time cloud posture review
options.D: Nessus for vulnerability and compliance scanning across general systems

questions.target: 2.2 Cloud infrastructure assessment tools / Scout Suite
questions.stem: An assessor needs a broad, point-in-time configuration review across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud using one open-source cloud-auditing tool that gathers configuration data through provider APIs. Which tool best fits?

options.A: Pacu for offensive testing of AWS permissions and attack paths
options.B: AWS Config for managed compliance evaluation inside AWS accounts
options.C: Nessus for general vulnerability and compliance assessment
options.D: Scout Suite for multi-cloud security posture assessment

questions.stem: A CVSS 9.8 vulnerability affects an isolated test appliance with no sensitive data. A CVSS 8.1 vulnerability affects an Internet-facing identity server and has reliable public exploitation. Which should be remediated first?

options.A: The identity server because exposure, exploitability, and asset criticality raise practical risk
options.B: The test appliance because its higher base score is the strongest available severity signal
options.C: Treat both as equal priority because both ratings indicate substantial technical severity
options.D: The test appliance because isolated systems provide less telemetry during exploitation

questions.stem: A vulnerability is exploitable over the network without credentials, but exploitation succeeds only after a user opens a crafted document. Which CVSS factor captures that dependency?

options.A: Privileges Required
options.B: User Interaction
options.C: Attack Complexity
options.D: Scope

questions.stem: A scanner reports that TLS 1.0 is enabled on a load balancer. Repeated manual handshakes using TLS 1.0 fail, and the active configuration permits TLS 1.2 and 1.3. How should the finding be handled?

options.A: Treat it as a true positive until the vendor publishes a scanner plugin update
options.B: Classify it as a false negative because the scanner detected a protocol that was blocked
options.C: Document the validation evidence and classify the scanner result as a false positive
options.D: Accept the risk because cryptographic findings cannot be validated manually

questions.stem: A penetration test successfully exploits an outdated service that the weekly vulnerability scan did not report. What does this most directly indicate about the scan result?

options.A: The penetration test produced a false positive because the scanner did not agree
options.B: The asset should be removed from future scans to prevent inconsistent findings
options.C: The CVSS score should be reduced because detection coverage was incomplete
options.D: The scanner produced a false negative for the exploitable condition

questions.stem: A vendor discloses an actively exploited zero-day in a service used by the organization. No patch exists. One instance is Internet-facing; another is isolated in a lab. What should vulnerability management do first?

options.A: Prioritize exposure reduction and compensating controls for the Internet-facing instance
options.B: Wait for a CVSS base score before making any containment changes
options.C: Take the isolated lab instance offline before reviewing the exposed production service
options.D: Suppress the finding until a vendor patch can be included in the normal cycle

questions.stem: A medium-severity privilege-escalation flaw affects a domain controller, while a high-severity denial-of-service flaw affects a disposable kiosk. Which data should drive priority beyond the scanner scores?

options.A: The alphabetical order of affected hostnames and vulnerability titles
options.B: Asset criticality, exposure path, exploitability, and business impact
options.C: The number of plugins each scanner used during discovery
options.D: The physical distance between the scanner and each target

questions.stem: A web application accepts a user-supplied image URL. An attacker submits http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ and the server returns cloud instance metadata. Which vulnerability pattern best explains the behavior?

options.A: Cross-site request forgery
options.B: Remote file inclusion
options.C: Server-side request forgery
options.D: Persistent cross-site scripting

questions.stem: A user changes /api/invoices/4821 to /api/invoices/4822 and receives another customer's invoice while remaining logged in as the original user. Which remediation most directly addresses the flaw?

options.A: Encode invoice numbers before displaying them in HTML
options.B: Add a CSRF token to the invoice download request
options.C: Require stronger transport security and client certificate validation for API connections
options.D: Enforce object-level authorization on each requested resource

questions.stem: An application builds SELECT statements by concatenating a username from an HTTP request. Which code change most directly reduces SQL injection risk?

options.A: Use parameterized queries with bound values
options.B: HTML-encode the query result before rendering
options.C: Store the database password in a secrets manager
options.D: Add a stricter session idle timeout

questions.stem: A comments page stores user input and later inserts it into other users' HTML pages. A stored script executes in visitors' browsers. Which change most directly addresses the vulnerable output path?

options.A: Add a CSRF token to the comment-submission form
options.B: Apply context-appropriate output encoding when rendering comments
options.C: Move the database to a segmented network
options.D: Hash the comment text before storing it

questions.stem: A banking site relies on a user's existing session cookie. A malicious page causes the browser to submit a funds-transfer POST to the bank without the user's intent. Which control most directly mitigates this attack?

options.A: Rely on SameSite cookie settings to reduce cross-site cookie submission
options.B: Require transaction reauthentication without binding the request to an anti-CSRF value
options.C: Require an anti-CSRF token that is validated with the authenticated request context
options.D: Validate the Origin or Referer header as the primary request-forgery defense

questions.stem: A download endpoint accepts file=quarterly.pdf. Changing it to file=../../../../etc/passwd returns local system content. Which corrective approach best addresses the flaw?

options.A: Reject path strings containing ../ sequences before joining them to the storage path
options.B: Map public file identifiers to server-side object names rather than accepting raw paths
options.C: Run the download service in a restricted filesystem namespace to limit traversal impact
options.D: Resolve requested files within an approved storage root and reject traversal outside it

questions.stem: A critical patch fixes remote code execution on a revenue system, but the vendor notes a possible compatibility issue with one plugin. What is the best remediation sequence?

options.A: Test the patch and rollback steps, deploy in an approved window, and validate remediation and service health
options.B: Deploy directly to the cluster and prepare rollback steps if compatibility problems appear
options.C: Deploy compensating network controls first and postpone testing until the next standard patch window
options.D: Deploy to one node without a rollback plan and rely on health monitoring before wider rollout

questions.stem: A medical device cannot be patched for six months because the vendor requires recertification. Security can restrict network paths, monitor protocol use, and enforce jump-host access. Which response best describes this plan?

options.A: Accept the risk because a vendor restriction removes organizational responsibility
options.B: Mitigate the risk with compensating controls while tracking the patch exception
options.C: Transfer the risk by moving the device to a different internal subnet
options.D: Avoid the risk by leaving the device online but excluding it from future scans

questions.stem: External discovery finds an Internet-facing management interface that is not in the asset inventory and has no documented business owner. What should happen first?

options.A: Add the hostname to the next quarterly vulnerability report and leave exposure unchanged
options.B: Increase the interface's session timeout so administrators have more time to investigate
options.C: Validate ownership and necessity, then remove or restrict exposure if it is not required
options.D: Run fuzzing against the interface from the Internet before notifying the service owner

questions.target: 3.1 Cyber kill chain for intrusion phase analysis
questions.stem: An intrusion timeline shows spear phishing, exploit execution, malware installation, command-and-control establishment, and data theft. The team wants to identify where an earlier defensive action could have interrupted the progression. Which framework best supports that phase-oriented analysis?

options.A: The Diamond Model focused on adversary-victim-infrastructure-capability relationships
options.B: CVSS focused on vulnerability severity and exploit characteristics
options.C: CIS Benchmarks focused on secure system configuration
options.D: A cyber kill chain model for phase progression

questions.stem: Analysts link the same phishing domain and command-and-control host to two malware families targeting different subsidiaries. They want to reason about relationships among adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim. Which framework best fits?

options.A: The Diamond Model for intrusion relationships
options.B: A cyber kill chain model for phase progression
options.C: OWASP Testing Guide for application-layer testing
options.D: MITRE ATT&CK for adversary behavior mapping

questions.stem: EDR records credential dumping, remote service use, and scheduled-task creation across several hosts. The SOC wants to map these observed behaviors to a common adversary-technique taxonomy and identify detection gaps. Which framework best fits?

options.A: Cyber kill chain for intrusion phase analysis
options.B: MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping
options.C: The Diamond Model for intrusion relationships
options.D: OWASP Testing Guide for web security testing

questions.stem: A team is planning a broad security test covering people, processes, physical considerations, wireless, telecommunications, and data networks rather than only web applications. Which methodology is the closer fit?

options.A: OWASP Testing Guide for application-layer testing
options.B: MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping
options.C: OSSTMM methodology for broad security testing
options.D: Cyber kill chain for intrusion phase analysis

questions.target: 3.1 OWASP Testing Guide for application-layer testing
questions.stem: An assessor is building a structured test plan for authentication, session management, input validation, and authorization in a web application. Which reference is most directly applicable?

options.A: Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis
options.B: Cyber kill chain for intrusion phase analysis
options.C: NIST time synchronization guidance
options.D: OWASP Testing Guide for application-layer testing

questions.stem: A report states that an actor used PowerShell for execution, RDP for lateral movement, and scheduled tasks for persistence. Which use of this information is most appropriate?

options.A: Map the behaviors to ATT&CK techniques and compare them with existing telemetry and controls
options.B: Assign a CVSS score to the actor's overall campaign based on the number of techniques
options.C: Use the Diamond Model to calculate the malware's cryptographic hash
options.D: Use the kill chain to prove which named threat actor conducted the intrusion

questions.stem: A SIEM alert shows suspicious PowerShell on one endpoint. EDR then reveals the same user authenticated to three servers, two of which launched encoded PowerShell within minutes. What should the responder do next?

options.A: Contain the first endpoint while leaving the server activity as a separate investigation
options.B: Expand the incident scope by correlating identity and endpoint evidence across the affected systems
options.C: Reimage the three servers before preserving volatile or forensic evidence
options.D: Close the alert after confirming that PowerShell is an approved administrative tool

questions.stem: An analyst creates a forensic disk image for an investigation that may become a legal matter. Which step most directly demonstrates that the image has not changed since acquisition?

options.A: Rename the image file after each analyst completes a review
options.B: Compress the image before hashing so storage use remains predictable
options.C: Calculate and record cryptographic hashes at acquisition and verification points
options.D: Store the image on the same workstation used to examine the original disk

questions.stem: A drive image is transferred from an incident responder to an outside forensic specialist. What documentation is most important to preserve chain of custody?

options.A: The analyst's preferred forensic tool and workstation screen resolution
options.B: The vulnerability scanner version used elsewhere in the incident
options.C: The business owner's estimate of the affected system's replacement cost
options.D: Transferor, recipient, time, location, and the evidence identifier or seal condition

questions.stem: During an investigation, counsel instructs the team not to delete mailbox, chat, and endpoint records for a group of custodians even though normal retention would expire. What should the response team do?

options.A: Preserve the identified records under legal hold and document the scope and custodians
options.B: Continue normal deletion because retention schedules take precedence over investigations
options.C: Export summary records and allow normal retention to remove the underlying data
options.D: Reclassify the incident as a vulnerability-management event until litigation begins

questions.stem: A workstation is encrypting a shared drive and contacting a known ransomware command-and-control endpoint. What action should occur first if isolation is technically available?

options.A: Reimage the workstation before identifying the affected shares and credentials
options.B: Isolate the workstation from the network while preserving access needed for response
options.C: Delete the ransomware binary and reconnect the system to confirm that encryption stops
options.D: Wait for the full incident scope before taking any host-level containment action

questions.stem: A compromised application server processes time-critical transactions. Immediate shutdown would stop suspected attacker access but also halt customer payments. Which response is best?

options.A: Shut down the server because containment decisions should not consider operational impact
options.B: Leave the server unchanged until eradication can be completed in a single maintenance event
options.C: Choose a containment method that limits attacker access while accounting for transaction impact and documented business priorities
options.D: Delete suspicious files first so the application can remain online without further analysis

questions.stem: A compromised web server has been isolated, malicious persistence removed, credentials rotated, and the vulnerable component patched. What should occur before returning it to normal service?

options.A: Destroy the incident evidence so the restored server starts with a clean investigative record
options.B: Remove network monitoring to reduce false positives during the recovery period
options.C: Close the incident after eradication and address service validation during normal operations
options.D: Validate that the remediation is effective and monitor the restored system for recurrence

questions.stem: An endpoint has multiple unknown persistence mechanisms, altered security tooling, and uncertain system integrity. Which recovery approach is most defensible?

options.A: Reimage from a trusted baseline and restore validated data rather than attempting piecemeal cleanup
options.B: Delete the known malicious files and assume the remaining operating system is trustworthy
options.C: Keep the system isolated indefinitely so forensic uncertainty does not affect recovery
options.D: Return the endpoint to the user after changing the local account password

questions.stem: An analyst finds an Internet-exposed server running an active web shell. Memory may contain attacker commands and connections, but the host is still being used for lateral movement. What is the best response principle?

options.A: Complete full forensic acquisition before changing connectivity so evidence collection is comprehensive
options.B: Balance rapid containment with targeted volatile evidence collection when it can be done without materially extending attacker access
options.C: Power off the server first and rely on disk evidence for subsequent analysis
options.D: Leave the server connected until the root cause is proven so the attacker behavior can be observed longer

questions.stem: A tabletop shows that analysts disagree about who can isolate a production database and when executive approval is required. What preparation improvement most directly addresses the gap?

options.A: Revise the incident-response plan with higher-level roles but no system-specific authority
options.B: Add a contact roster and escalation matrix without defining containment authority
options.C: Update the playbook with containment authority, escalation criteria, and decision paths
options.D: Create a database recovery runbook without defining incident containment approvals

questions.stem: Executives, legal, communications, IT, and security walk through a simulated ransomware event using injects but do not touch production systems. What is the primary value of the exercise?

options.A: Measure endpoint detection accuracy against live malware samples
options.B: Prove that backup restoration will meet recovery objectives under production load
options.C: Determine the CVSS score of the ransomware used in the scenario
options.D: Validate roles, decisions, communications, and procedural gaps before a real incident

questions.stem: Ransomware containment requires taking a critical order-processing system offline. The response team needs the documented recovery sequence, alternate processing arrangements, and restoration priorities after containment. Which preparation artifact should it consult?

options.A: BC/DR documentation describing recovery procedures, dependencies, and restoration priorities
options.B: The incident-response plan describing team roles and escalation contacts
options.C: The business impact analysis identifying criticality, dependencies, and outage consequences
options.D: The service-level agreement describing provider support and maintenance commitments

questions.stem: After restoring service, the team determines the initial compromise used a stolen contractor token that remained valid after contract termination. Which follow-up action best reflects root cause analysis?

options.A: Block the attacker's IP address and treat the incident cause as fully remediated
options.B: Trace why deprovisioning failed and correct the identity lifecycle control that allowed token persistence
options.C: Increase endpoint scan frequency because the intrusion involved a compromised account
options.D: Replace the affected server hardware because credentials were used to access it

questions.stem: The incident is closed, but responders found that firewall requests took three hours because ownership was unclear. What should the team do with this finding?

options.A: Remove it from the final report because the technical containment eventually succeeded
options.B: Treat it as a vulnerability false positive because no software flaw caused the delay
options.C: Record it in lessons learned and assign a measurable process improvement with an owner
options.D: Wait for another incident to confirm that the delay is reproducible before changing process

questions.stem: A monthly report lists 1,800 findings but does not show affected business services, exploitability, age, or remediation owners. Executives cannot tell what needs attention. Which change would most improve the report?

options.A: Add detailed scanner output and plugin evidence as the primary executive decision material
options.B: Sort findings alphabetically by vulnerability title and remove asset context
options.C: Report the average CVSS score and omit business-service and ownership context
options.D: Group findings by business risk and priority with affected assets, owners, mitigation, and aging

questions.stem: The same critical configuration finding reappears on newly built servers each month after remediation teams fix existing hosts. What should reporting emphasize?

options.A: The recurrence trend, affected build path, likely configuration cause, and current host impact
options.B: The current CVSS score without comparing previous reporting periods
options.C: The remediation ticket closure rate without showing why new systems inherit the condition
options.D: The scanner confidence score without comparing affected cohorts or recurrence over time

questions.stem: A PCI-scoped environment has several overdue high-risk findings. Management asks whether remediation performance meets required internal and external obligations. What should the analyst provide?

options.A: A threat-hunting report listing unrelated indicators observed elsewhere in the enterprise
options.B: A compliance-oriented report mapping affected scope, findings, status, exceptions, and required deadlines
options.C: A packet capture from the most recently scanned payment server
options.D: A software inventory that omits vulnerability and remediation status

questions.stem: A legacy system cannot be patched without interrupting a 24x7 manufacturing process, and replacement is scheduled in four months. Which reporting approach is best?

options.A: Mark the finding remediated because a replacement project has been funded
options.B: Remove the system from vulnerability reports until the replacement is complete
options.C: Document the inhibitor, interim compensating controls, owner, target date, and accepted escalation path
options.D: Raise the CVSS base score so the scanner reflects the manufacturing impact

questions.stem: The security team aims to remediate critical vulnerabilities within seven days, but a managed service contract requires the provider to deploy approved critical patches within ten days. Which statement best reflects the two commitments?

options.A: The seven-day target is an SLA, while the ten-day provider term is an internal SLO
options.B: Both are CVSS temporal metrics because they change over time
options.C: The seven-day target is an SLO, while the ten-day provider term is a KPI without contractual force
options.D: The seven-day target is an internal SLO, while the ten-day provider obligation is an SLA requirement

questions.stem: Critical findings fell from 120 to 40, but median age rose from 12 to 55 days and several systems remain repeatedly vulnerable. What should the analyst communicate?

options.A: The count improved, but aging and recurrence indicate unresolved remediation-process risk
options.B: The program improved overall because the total finding count decreased
options.C: The older findings should be excluded from trends because they predate the current month
options.D: The scanner should be retuned until the median age matches the lower finding count

questions.stem: A critical vulnerability affects an Internet-facing application owned by a business unit, operated by a managed provider, and governed by a security exception. Who should receive the remediation communication?

options.A: The vulnerability-management team alone because it discovered the condition
options.B: The accountable service owner, technical operator, security/risk stakeholders, and exception approver as appropriate
options.C: A broad employee distribution so other teams can identify potential technical owners
options.D: The software vendor alone because application owners cannot change third-party code

questions.stem: A business unit repeatedly creates public cloud storage despite remediation tickets because its deployment template defaults to public access. Which action plan is most likely to prevent recurrence?

options.A: Continue closing each exposed bucket individually without changing the build process
options.B: Reduce scan frequency so duplicate findings do not dominate monthly reports
options.C: Correct the deployment template and reinforce the required configuration with the responsible teams
options.D: Move the findings to an incident report because recurrence proves malicious intent

questions.stem: An analyst confirms customer records were accessed by an unauthorized account, but the total number of affected records is still unknown. What should happen next?

options.A: Delay declaration until the exact record count and root cause are known
options.B: Close the alert because uncertainty prevents reliable incident classification
options.C: Notify customers directly before legal, privacy, and communications stakeholders are engaged
options.D: Declare and escalate according to the incident criteria while continuing scope analysis

questions.stem: A technical report contains process trees, hashes, firewall logs, and forensic timestamps. Senior leadership needs a one-page update. What should the executive summary emphasize?

options.A: Business impact, current scope, response status, material risks, and decisions required
options.B: The detailed attacker command sequence and associated forensic artifacts
options.C: The complete chain-of-custody record for each acquired artifact
options.D: The syntax used by analysts to query the SIEM during detection

questions.stem: Firewall events use UTC, endpoint logs use local time, and a cloud service exports ISO timestamps with offsets. What should the analyst do before presenting a unified incident timeline?

options.A: Sort events lexicographically exactly as exported from each source
options.B: Normalize timestamps to a common reference and retain source-time context
options.C: Convert source times into the analyst's local zone and present that transformed timeline
options.D: Exclude sources that do not already use the organization's preferred time zone

questions.stem: A ransomware incident disrupts customer services and a reporter contacts an engineer for comment. Which communication path is most appropriate?

options.A: Allow the engineer to describe current forensic hypotheses because rapid transparency reduces speculation
options.B: Ask the threat actor for approval before discussing the incident publicly
options.C: Route external statements through legal and public relations using verified facts from the response team
options.D: Publish the raw incident channel so customers can follow investigation progress directly

questions.stem: An incident may trigger a statutory notification deadline, but forensic scope is still evolving. What should the incident lead do first?

options.A: Wait until root cause analysis is complete because reporting before certainty creates legal risk
options.B: Send early notices to broadly relevant regulators before determining jurisdictional scope
options.C: Exclude uncertain affected populations from internal records until the final report is issued
options.D: Engage legal and compliance stakeholders to determine applicable obligations and preserve deadline-relevant facts

questions.stem: A financially motivated intrusion includes extortion and confirmed theft of regulated customer data. Leadership is considering law-enforcement involvement. Which factor should guide the decision?

options.A: Established incident policy plus legal, jurisdictional, evidentiary, and business considerations
options.B: Whether the malware hash appears in at least three public reputation services
options.C: Whether the vulnerability used in the intrusion has a CVSS score above 9.0
options.D: Whether the attacker used an IP address registered outside the country

questions.stem: A phishing message led to token theft. Investigation also finds that conditional-access policy excluded the affected legacy application. How should the final report treat these findings?

options.A: Select one cause and omit the other so management receives a single unambiguous explanation
options.B: Distinguish the initial attack path from control gaps that enabled or amplified the incident
options.C: Treat the phishing message as the sole root cause because it occurred first in the timeline
options.D: Treat the policy exclusion as unrelated because the attacker still needed a phishing message

questions.stem: An incident report recommends 'improve security monitoring' after an attacker used newly created service-account credentials for lateral movement. Which revision would be more actionable?

options.A: Replace the recommendation with a catalog of telemetry sources used during the investigation
options.B: Recommend blocking the attacker's IP as the primary long-term control for credential misuse
options.C: Specify telemetry, detection logic, ownership, and a validation measure for anomalous service-account use
options.D: State that analysts should be more vigilant without changing tooling or process

questions.stem: A SOC detects incidents faster after new analytics are deployed, but containment still takes several hours because approvals are manual. Which metric pattern best reflects the change?

options.A: MTTD and response time should move together because both depend on alert-processing speed
options.B: Alert volume should decrease as faster detection removes duplicate downstream alerts
options.C: CVSS temporal scores decrease because the SOC detects incidents sooner
options.D: MTTD improves while response or remediation time remains comparatively high
